_comment: Char ceilings for the always-loaded canon and its companions. A ceiling is a MAX: shrinking always passes. Raising one needs --update in its own justified commit, with a reason. See scripts/check_claudemd_budget.py. CLAUDE.md is loaded into EVERY session, so its size is a standing tax on all work; it was 349,512 chars before the v1.130.0 canon/changelog split and is budgeted at 82,000 to leave real working room without letting the changelog creep back in. The archive is budgeted generously because it is a grep target that is never auto-loaded - it is listed only so that 'shrink CLAUDE.md' cannot be satisfied by moving weight somewhere nobody is watching. ARCHIVE CEILING RAISED 420,000 -> 430,000 (v1.145.14). Three consecutive commits (v1.145.10, v1.145.13, v1.146.0) each had to compress genuine post-mortem narrative to fit, and v1.145.13 evicted part of the entry it superseded and recorded that 'shaving is spent'. Compressing the record to satisfy a cap degrades the exact thing the cap exists to protect. The reason for capping the archive is displacement - so that 'shrink CLAUDE.md' cannot be satisfied by moving canon somewhere nobody watches - and that reason is unaffected here: the archive is a grep target, never auto-loaded, so its size is not a per-session tax. CLAUDE.md's own 82,000 is untouched and is the ceiling that actually matters. Raised by 10,000 (2.4%), not opened up, so the next raise is still a deliberate act. RAISED AGAIN AT v1.147.1, both files, for two DIFFERENT reasons - measured, not estimated. docs/Neural.md: origin/dev stood at 39,997 of 40,000 - THREE chars of headroom - and v1.147.0's pane-pager entry took it to 40,830 before the MC work touched it at all. A behaviour doc that is actively maintained cannot live on 3 chars; the next writer's only options were to compress someone else's paragraph or skip documenting their change, and the second is what actually happens. Raised to 43,000 (+7.5%). docs/Changelog-Archive.md: the v1.145.14 raise to 430,000 left 919 chars by the time v1.148.0's post-mortem was written - one entry of headroom, i.e. a ceiling-raise commit per entry, which turns a growth SIGNAL into a per-entry tax and pressures writers to under-document exactly the near-misses worth recording. Raised to 445,000 (+3.5%). Neither is opened up: both remain deliberate acts, and CLAUDE.md's 82,000 - the ceiling that is a per-session tax and the only one that truly matters - is untouched at 70,657.
